_comment: The technician of a scene is male (actor 6, Technician male) or female (actor 7, Technician female); the mission picks one at random in app mode and publishes it in L:HMC_TECH_SEX. FRA.* are the lines of the technician at the start of a flight (fuel, GPU, logbook, greetings) and SARA.* the lines at the return to base; each has options for both sexes (m, f) written as different sketches. The crew lines that greet or answer the technician (CPL.23 and so on) do not depend on the sex: they use {@TECH}, the name of the technician (random or typed by the user) or the word Technician when there is none, and half of the options have no name at all. {@PLT} is the name of the pilot, or Pilot. Options of a tight message (the mission waits a short time after it) are of a similar length.

m: If you need refueling please ask.
Morning. If you want fuel, just say so.
Need any fuel today? Just ask.
f: Hi. Let me know if you need refueling.
Good morning. Do you need any fuel today?
Fuel is available whenever you want it, just ask.

m: Fuel is as you requested.
Fuel loaded as requested.
You have the fuel you asked for.
f: Fuel is as you requested.
All done: the fuel you asked for is on board.
Refueling complete, as requested.

m: Fuel tanks are almost full.
The tanks are nearly full.
You are almost full on fuel.
f: Fuel tanks are almost full.
Tanks are nearly full, you are good to go.
You have a nearly full tank.

m: Refueling has not been performed and fuel level is low.
No refueling was done, so the fuel level is low.
Careful, you did not refuel and the level is low.
f: Refueling has not been performed and fuel level is low.
Heads up: no fuel was added and the level is low.
The tanks are low, refueling was not performed.

m: GPU disconnected. Ready to go. Good day.
Power unit disconnected, you are ready to go. Good day.
GPU is off, all set. Have a good flight.
f: GPU disconnected. You are ready to go. Have a good day.
External power removed. All set, good flight.
Power unit is clear, you can go. Good day.

m: {@PLT}, the helicopter is ready for flight. The logbook is completed and signed.
The helicopter is ready, and the logbook is signed.
Logbook completed and signed, the helicopter is clear for flight.
f: {@PLT}, the helicopter is ready for flight. I have completed and signed the logbook.
Everything is checked and the logbook is signed, you are ready.
The aircraft is clear for flight. Logbook is signed.

m: Good morning, everyone. Ready for the mission?
Hi all. Ready for today?
Morning, team. Everything ready for the mission?
f: Good morning, everyone. Ready for the mission?
Hello team. Are you ready for today?
Morning, all. Ready to go?

m: Ready to provide external power at your request.
I can supply external power whenever you want.
Power unit ready, just say when.
f: Ready to connect external power when you want.
Say the word and I give you external power.
External power is ready at your request.

m: Aircraft requires inspection. Do not depart until maintenance releases it.
The aircraft needs an inspection. Please wait for the maintenance release before departing.
f: The aircraft needs an inspection. Please do not depart until maintenance releases it.
Inspection required on this aircraft. Wait for the maintenance release before you go.

m: Bye, see you tomorrow.
See you later. Have a good evening.
Take care, guys. See you tomorrow.
f: Bye, see you tomorrow.
See you tomorrow, take care.
Bye everyone, see you tomorrow.

m: How was the mission? Everything good with the helicopter?
Good mission? Any problem with the helicopter?
f: How was the last mission? Was the helicopter all right?
How did the mission go? Any trouble with the helicopter?

m: Fine, thanks.
All good, thanks.
I am fine, thank you.
f: Fine, thanks.
I am fine, thank you.
All good, thanks.

m: Do not worry, the helicopter is in good hands. It will be ready for the next mission.
Leave it to me: the helicopter will be ready for the next mission.
Do not worry about the helicopter. I will have it ready for the next mission.
f: Do not worry; the helicopter is in good hands and will be ready for the next mission.
Relax, I take care of the helicopter. It will be ready for the next one.
Do not worry, I will get the helicopter ready for the next mission.

m: Hey, guys.
Hi all, welcome back.
Hello, team.
f: Hi, guys.
Hello, everyone.
Hi team, welcome back.

m: It looks like I have a lot of work to do.
Well, plenty of work for me today.
I will be busy with this one for a while.
f: It looks like I have a lot of work to do.
Looks like I have plenty of work ahead of me.
I see I will be busy with this helicopter.

m: Tomorrow there is a barbecue at the base. Would you like to join us?
A few of us are going to the pub tomorrow. Do you want to come?
f: Tomorrow there is a good restaurant just outside. Would you like to go?
There is a nice restaurant just outside tomorrow. Do you want to join me?

m: What did you do to my helicopter?
Hey, what have you done to the helicopter?
f: What did you do to the helicopter?
Hey, what happened to the helicopter?

o: That was a hard landing. {@TECH} will not be happy.
That was a hard landing. Maintenance will not be happy.
Hard landing. {@TECH} will not like this one.
That was a hard landing. Expect a long look from maintenance.
Hi {@TECH}, how are you? The helicopter is good, but it needs refuelling.
Hello! The helicopter is good, but it needs refuelling.
Hi {@TECH}. All good with the helicopter, but it needs fuel.
Hello, how are you? The helicopter is fine but needs refuelling.
Hi {@TECH}, I am sorry, we have some bad news for you.
Hi, I am sorry. We have some bad news for you.
Sorry {@TECH}, we have some bad news.
I am sorry, we have bad news about the helicopter.
